items.q: What's the difference between isolate and concentrate?
items.a: Isolate is filtered further, so it's higher in protein and lower in fat, carbs and lactose than concentrate — leaner and easier to digest.
Within 30–60 minutes after training is ideal, but any time you need to top up protein works — between meals or as a quick breakfast.

items.q: Is it okay if I'm lactose-sensitive?
items.a: Isolate is very low in lactose, so many people who react to regular whey tolerate it well. It does contain milk, so avoid it if you're allergic.
No added sugar — it's sweetened naturally with stevia leaf extract, with flavour from natural sources (real cocoa in the chocolate).
